title: Saung gauk (Burmese arched harp)
summary: The saung gauk is the arched harp of Myanmar. A red lacquered boat-shaped body carries a gracefully curving neck hung with silk tassels, and thirteen silk strings run from the neck across a stretched hide. Its soft, clear voice carries sung court songs and lively dance tunes.
howToPlay: Thirteen silk strings are drawn from the curved neck down to the hide: low notes on one side, high notes on the other.
Watch a bead glide down a string; pluck that string just as the bead reaches the hide.
Begin with the slow falling-note air, then try the quicker dance tune and the answering phrases.
Silk strings ring softly and fade slowly, so let each note speak before the next one.
rules: Thirteen strings are tuned to a seven-note scale close to the major scale, rising across about two octaves.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
Each song is played twice through.
Slow songs reward steady, even plucking; quick tunes reward a light, ready hand.
A faint ring and shimmer on a string show that it has sounded.
heritageNote: Harps like the saung gauk appear in Burmese carvings and paintings for well over a thousand years. It is the only arched harp still played everyday in Southeast Asia, accompanying singers in classical songs.
